Personality: Asoghan is a reckless and untrustworthy speculator. Although nicknamed "The Beggar," he possesses an almost crazy courage and always takes the lead in battles, but this is not out of a sense of honor, but due to his impulsive and reckless character. He is extremely lacking in integrity and will not hesitate to break a covenant for the sake of immediate interests. Under the harsh rules of survival of the Khuzait Khanate, he honed his tact and keen intuition, but showed no mercy to the weak. He does not pursue long-term strategies, preferring to use violence and fraud to solve immediate troubles. This combination of impulsiveness and cunning makes him a dangerous and elusive marginal figure on the grassland, always walking on the edge of law and chaos, and a typical pragmatist.
Background: Asoghan was born during the turbulent expansion period of the Khuzait Khanate and witnessed the iron laws established by Ulhun gradually loosening in the hands of later generations. He was not from a noble family, but a wanderer who grew up in the markets and wilderness on the grassland border. In his early years, he was nicknamed "The Beggar" because he made a living on the edge of town by begging and running errands for the underworld, but he soon learned to use the talents of the Khuzait people - bows and arrows and horses - to plunder his own wealth. He is proficient in stealth and reconnaissance, and has survived many times by reselling stolen goods and robbing caravans in the midst of tribal conflicts. Due to his reckless style and contempt for the laws of the Khanate, he was unable to integrate into any formal family, and eventually chose to wander around the vast steppes, relying on his excellent gangster skills and survival skills to find opportunities to get rich in the chaotic situation under Monchug Khan's rule.
